purpose: Repository-anchored inventory of Aeon's two architectural clocks. Written before the corrected mathematical spec assigns meaning to C_1 or C_2.

fast_clock.quoted_text: fast clock (per token, within a K-window w; conditioning state = h_{w-1})

slow_clock.quoted_text: slow clock (once at end of window w)

fast_clock.cadence_definition: exactly once per input token index i, i in [start, end) inside each K-window w

concrete_implementations: aeon/substrate/matrix_cell.py::MatrixCell — per-batch matrix state S of shape (H, N, N)

fast_clock.update_trigger: the inner for-loop `for i in range(start, end):` in aeon/hybrid.py:154-158; runs once per token index
fast_clock.relative_rate: K ticks per one slow-clock tick
fast_clock.interaction_with_recursion: the fast-clock READOUTS r_i are aggregated by `mean_i r_i` at aeon/hybrid.py:160 and then projected as `s_w = self.s_proj(mean_readout)` at 161 to become one of the slow-clock inputs
fast_clock.interaction_with_transformer: the fast-clock input x_i is `emb_proj(emb_i) + cond_proj(h_{w-1})` at aeon/hybrid.py:151-155 — the transformer embedding stream contributes emb_i and the SLOW clock's held state h_{w-1} conditions each fast tick
fast_clock.configuration_fields: no direct config knob — the fast clock runs once per token by definition of the token loop; the number of fast ticks per slow tick is K
tests_asserting_fast_clock_semantics: tests/test_substrate_port.py — port contract shape / dtype tests
tests/test_recursion_topology.py::test_recursion_step_called_once_per_window (indirect — proves slow clock is NOT per-token)

slow_clock.cadence_definition: exactly once at the END of every K-window; num_windows = ceil(T / K)

state_variables_governed.recursion_h: aeon/recursion.py::RecursionJoiner.h_init -> (H_rec,) fp32; carried between slow ticks by aeon/hybrid.py:175 — `h, c = self.recursion.step(...)`
state_variables_governed.recursion_c: same, second component of the joiner tick
state_variables_governed.shared_broadcast_h_cond: aeon/hybrid.py:150 — `h_cond = h` at the START of each window w; captured before the tick and rebroadcast to every fast token within window w via `inject_cols.append(h_cond)` at 158
state_variables_governed.transformer_write_inject: aeon/hybrid.py: the stacked inject_cols vector is applied at the transformer.inject(...) call after the loop

slow_clock.update_trigger: the outer for-loop `for w in range(num_windows):` at aeon/hybrid.py:146; each iteration ends with the single call `h, c = self.recursion.step(s_w.float(), t_w.float(), h.detach(), c.detach(), e=...)` at aeon/hybrid.py:175-177
slow_clock.interaction_with_recursion_joiner: the slow-clock tick IS the RecursionJoiner call. Inputs (s, t, h, c, optional e) map to (substrate-projection, transformer-K-th-readout, previous h, previous c, window-mean embedding). Governed by the σ<margin_h, σ<margin_c certificate.
slow_clock.interaction_with_substrate: the slow-clock tick READS the substrate through `s_w = s_proj(mean_i r_i)` (aeon/hybrid.py:160-161) and, at end-of-tick, DETACHES the substrate state via `self.substrate.detach_state()` at aeon/hybrid.py:178 (truncated BPTT — design note D2)
slow_clock.interaction_with_transformer_stream: the K-th (end-of-window) transformer readout is picked at `t_w = t_all[:, end - 1, :]` (aeon/hybrid.py:162); the slow-clock output `h_{w-1}` is broadcast into every fast-token position via inject_cols and written to hidden via `transformer.inject(hidden, inject_signal)` at the end of the forward
configuration_fields: model.margin_h / model.margin_c (σ-certificate constants) in every config
implementation_files_and_lines: aeon/hybrid.py:146-178 (outer window loop, slow-clock tick + substrate detach)

coupling_between_the_two_clocks.fast_conditions_on_slow: aeon/hybrid.py:150-155 — h_{w-1} conditions every fast tick within window w via cond_proj
coupling_between_the_two_clocks.slow_carries_fast_boundary_detach: aeon/hybrid.py:176 — h.detach()/c.detach() into recursion.step; and 178 — substrate.detach_state() (truncated BPTT per D2)
coupling_between_the_two_clocks.slow_writes_transformer_via_inject: aeon/hybrid.py:23 (docstring) — logits = lm_head(hidden + γ · write_proj(inject_signal)); inject_signal[window w tokens] = h_{w-1}

modules_intentionally_frozen_by_existing.notes: the correction order (§10 previous EN-TRAIN spec) required identifying modules intentionally frozen by existing design. Repository search finds no explicit `requires_grad_(False)` calls in aeon/hybrid.py, aeon/recursion.py, or aeon/substrate/*. Every trainable parameter is trainable by default at construction. Only local scopes use `.detach()` for truncated BPTT (which is a per-forward autograd choice, not a permanent freeze). No exemption is claimed.

explicit_evidence.hybrid_freeze_backbone_arg: aeon/hybrid.py:73 — HybridModel(freeze_backbone: bool = False, ...) — DEFAULTS TO FALSE and the P2 checkpoint at runs/aeon_lbc1_P2/final.pt was trained with the default (see docs/training/p2_evidence.json)

clocks_summary: Aeon's two architectural clocks in this repository are the FAST CLOCK (per-token substrate.step inside each K-window, aeon/hybrid.py:154-158) and the SLOW CLOCK (per-K-window recursion.step + one shared broadcast + transformer inject, aeon/hybrid.py:146-178, aeon/recursion.py:148). K = 16 fixed. No formal C_1 / C_2 symbols appear in the repository; the corrected mathematical spec at docs/en_train/EN_TRAIN_CORRECTED_MATHEMATICAL_SPEC.md is the first place those bookkeeping symbols are introduced, and it binds them to the FAST and SLOW clocks in that order, without changing any of the above semantics.
